claim: ALC1 is recruited to DNA damage sites by poly(ADP-ribose) (PAR) chains deposited by PARP1/PARP2/HPF1.
source: The chromatin remodeler ALC1 is recruited to and activated by DNA damage-induced poly(ADP-ribose) (PAR) chains deposited by PARP1/PARP2/HPF1 upon detection of DNA lesions.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations to prior work throughout the manuscript.

claim: Loss of ALC1 confers synthetic lethality in homologous recombination-deficient cells.
source: ALC1 has emerged as a candidate drug target for cancer therapy as its loss confers synthetic lethality in homologous recombination-deficient cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations in the text (Abbott et al., 2020; Blessing et al., 2020; Hewitt et al., 2021; Juhász et al., 2020; Verma et al., 2021).

claim: Structure determination of ALC1 has been hindered by the requirement for PARylation and the heterogeneous nature of this post-translational modification.
source: However, structure-based drug design and molecular analysis of ALC1 have been hindered by the requirement for PARylation and the highly heterogeneous nature of this post-translational modification.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a motivation for the study.

claim: An ALC1 and PARylated nucleosome complex was reconstituted in vitro using PARP2 and HPF1.
source: Here, we reconstituted an ALC1 and PARylated nucleosome complex modified in vitro using PARP2 and HPF1.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding described in the abstract and detailed in the Results section.

claim: The ALC1-PARylated nucleosome complex was amenable to cryo-EM structure determination without cross-linking.
source: This complex was amenable to cryo-EM structure determination without cross-linking, which enabled visualization of several intermediate states of ALC1 from the recognition of the PARylated nucleosome to the tight binding and activation of the remodeler.
evidence: This is a key methodological achievement described in the abstract and demonstrated by the cryo-EM data presented.

claim: Multiple intermediate states of ALC1 were visualized from recognition of the PARylated nucleosome to tight binding and activation.
source: This complex was amenable to cryo-EM structure determination without cross-linking, which enabled visualization of several intermediate states of ALC1 from the recognition of the PARylated nucleosome to the tight binding and activation of the remodeler.
evidence: This is supported by the cryo-EM data and cryoDRGN analysis presented in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: Nucleosomal epitopes are important for productive remodeling by ALC1.
source: Functional biochemical assays with PARylated nucleosomes highlight the importance of nucleosomal epitopes for productive remodeling and suggest that ALC1 preferentially slides nucleosomes away from DNA breaks.
evidence: This is supported by the nucleosome sliding assays with mutant nucleosomes and ALC1 variants shown in Figure 5.

claim: ALC1 preferentially slides nucleosomes away from DNA breaks.
source: Functional biochemical assays with PARylated nucleosomes highlight the importance of nucleosomal epitopes for productive remodeling and suggest that ALC1 preferentially slides nucleosomes away from DNA breaks.
evidence: This is inferred from the sliding assay data showing directional bias based on PARylation site location.

claim: PARP1 and PARP2 are among the earliest components of the DNA damage response able to recognize DSBs.
source: One of the earliest components of the DNA damage response (DDR) able to recognize DSBs are the ADP-ribosyltransferases PARP1 and PARP2 (Krishnakumar and Kraus, 2010; Liu et al., 2017b; Lüscher et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: ALC1 uses its macro domain to bind to PAR produced by PARP1 and PARP2.
source: ALC1 uses its macro domain to bind to PAR (Ahel et al., 2009; Gottschalk et al., 2009) produced by PARP1 and PARP2.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: In the absence of DNA damage, the macro domain of ALC1 is abutted against its ATPase, which stabilizes an inactive conformation.
source: In the absence of DNA damage, the macro domain of ALC1 is abutted against its ATPase, which stabilizes an inactive conformation (Lehmann et al., 2017; Singh et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior structural and biochemical studies.

claim: The macro domain interacts predominantly with the C-terminal ATPase lobe.
source: Structural, biochemical, and in vivo analyses suggested that the macro domain interacts predominantly with the C-terminal ATPase lobe (Lehmann et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: PAR binding to the macro domain relieves auto-inhibition upon recruitment to DNA damage.
source: PAR binding to the macro domain relieves this auto-inhibition upon recruitment to DNA damage (Lehmann et al., 2017; Singh et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Full activation of ALC1 requires its linker to insert an Arg anchor motif into the nucleosome acidic patch.
source: Full activation of ALC1 requires its linker to insert an Arg anchor motif into the 'acidic patch' (AP) composed of negatively charged residues from histones H2A and H2B on both faces of the nucleosome (Lehmann et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work and confirmed by the structural data in this study.

claim: Cells lacking HPF1 display much-reduced survival after DNA damage.
source: A PARylation response leading to efficient repair requires HPF1 (Histone PARylation Factor 1), since cells lacking HPF1 display much-reduced survival after DNA damage (Bonfiglio et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Activation of ALC1 most likely requires nucleosomal histone PARylation in the presence of HPF1.
source: As a crucial step in the DNA damage response, activation of ALC1 therefore most likely requires nucleosomal histone PARylation in the presence of HPF1.
evidence: This is inferred from the requirement of HPF1 for histone PARylation and efficient DNA damage response.

claim: Inactivation of ALC1 sensitizes to clinical PARP inhibitors.
source: Recent studies have defined ALC1 as an attractive target for therapeutic intervention strategies in cancer as its inactivation sensitizes to clinical PARP inhibitors and confers synthetic lethality in homologous recombination-deficient cancer cells (Abbott et al., 2020; Blessing et al., 2020; Hewitt et al., 2021; Juhász et al., 2020; Verma et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to recent studies.

claim: Most high-resolution cryo-EM structures of nucleosome-bound chromatin remodelers were obtained with cross-linked complexes.
source: Most high-resolution cryo-EM structures of nucleosome-bound chromatin remodelers available to date were obtained with cross-linked complexes (Baker et al., 2021; Farnung et al., 2020; Farnung et al., 2017; Han et al., 2020; He et al., 2020; Meijing et al., 2019; Liu et al., 2017a; Patel et al., 2019; Wagner et al., 2020; Yan et al., 2019; Ye et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior structural studies.

claim: Several structures of non-cross-linked nucleosome-remodeler complexes have attained resolutions of around 4 Å.
source: Nonetheless, several structures of non-cross-linked nucleosome-remodeler complexes have attained resolutions of around 4 Å, sufficient to unambiguously assign secondary structure elements and to provide important mechanistic insights.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior structural studies.

claim: Three non-cross-linked structures were multi-subunit remodeling complexes.
source: Of these, three were multi-subunit remodeling complexes (Ayala et al., 2018; Eustermann et al., 2018; Willhoft et al., 2018) that may be overall more stable due to multiple interactions between catalytic and scaffolding subunits and the nucleosome, and the remaining three were single-subunit remodelers (Armache et al., 2019; Chittori et al., 2019; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior structural studies.

claim: Three non-cross-linked structures were single-subunit remodelers.
source: Of these, three were multi-subunit remodeling complexes (Ayala et al., 2018; Eustermann et al., 2018; Willhoft et al., 2018) that may be overall more stable due to multiple interactions between catalytic and scaffolding subunits and the nucleosome, and the remaining three were single-subunit remodelers (Armache et al., 2019; Chittori et al., 2019; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior structural studies.

claim: Cross-linking the ALC1-nucleosome complex may obscure key information on the recognition process.
source: Consequently, cross-linking the complex may obscure key information on the recognition process, by turning continuous conformational flexibility into a set of discrete states.
evidence: This is a reasoning provided by the authors for avoiding cross-linking.

claim: PARylated nucleosomes can be efficiently produced in vitro with PARP1 or PARP2 and HPF1.
source: Here, we show that PARylated nucleosomes can be efficiently produced in vitro with PARP1 or PARP2 and HPF1 and that such nucleosomes are the optimal substrate for ALC1.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding demonstrated by Western blot and functional assays.

claim: PARylated nucleosomes are the optimal substrate for ALC1.
source: Here, we show that PARylated nucleosomes can be efficiently produced in vitro with PARP1 or PARP2 and HPF1 and that such nucleosomes are the optimal substrate for ALC1.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the nucleosome sliding assays showing faster rates with PARylated nucleosomes.

claim: The isolated ATPase motor of ALC1 did not yield detectable binding to nucleosomes at concentrations suitable for cryo-EM.
source: At concentrations suitable for cryo-EM sample preparation, the isolated ATPase motor of ALC1 (ALC1cat) did not yield any detectable binding to nucleosomes in a gel shift assay (Figure 1A, lane 2).
evidence: This is shown by the EMSA data in Figure 1A.

claim: Full-length ALC1 bound to unmodified nucleosomes predominantly through non-specific interactions between its macro domain and DNA.
source: While an essentially full-length protein (ALC1fl) did bind to these nucleosomes (Figure 1A, lane 4), this binding predominantly originated from non-specific interactions between its macro domain (ALC1macro) and DNA (Figure 1A, lane 3), in agreement with our previous results (Lehmann et al., 2017).
evidence: This is shown by the EMSA data in Figure 1A and supported by citation to prior work.

claim: ALC1cat was unable to bind PARylated nucleosomes.
source: ALC1cat was still unable to bind the PARylated nucleosomes (Figure 1A, lanes 5 and 6)
evidence: This is shown by the EMSA data in Figure 1A.

claim: ALC1macro interacted strongly with PARylated nucleosomes.
source: while ALC1macro interacted strongly (Figure 1A, lane 7), consistent with the previously reported KD of ~11 nM for the interaction between ALC1macro and a tri-(ADP-ribose) model of PAR chains (Singh et al., 2017).
evidence: This is shown by the EMSA data in Figure 1A and supported by citation to prior work.

claim: The KD for the interaction between ALC1macro and tri-(ADP-ribose) is approximately 11 nM.
source: consistent with the previously reported KD of ~11 nM for the interaction between ALC1macro and a tri-(ADP-ribose) model of PAR chains (Singh et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from prior work.

claim: Binding of ALC1fl to PARylated nucleosomes resulted in a more defined pattern of shifted bands compared to unmodified nucleosomes.
source: The binding of ALC1fl to PARylated nucleosomes resulted in a more defined pattern of shifted bands (Figure 1A, lane 8 compared to lane 4), suggesting a complex with more restricted conformations.
evidence: This is shown by the EMSA data in Figure 1A.

claim: Nucleosome sliding by ALC1 was approximately 2.4-fold faster when PAR chains were attached to histones rather than exclusively to PARP1.
source: Nucleosome sliding by ALC1 was ~2.4-fold faster when PAR chains were attached to histones, rather than exclusively to PARP1 (Figure 1B), indicating that the PARylated nucleosome is the proper substrate of ALC1.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the FRET-based sliding assay data in Figure 1B.

claim: In-trans ADP-ribosylation of histones is critical to elicit a DNA damage response leading to successful repair and cellular viability.
source: This observation also corroborates the paradigm that in-trans ADP-ribosylation of histones, and not only auto-modification of PARP1 and PARP2, is critical to elicit a DNA damage response leading to successful repair and cellular viability (Bonfiglio et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work and corroborated by the sliding assay data.

claim: The H3 tail on the side of the DNA end bound by PARP2 is closest to its active site.
source: The structure of PARP2 and HPF1 bound to nucleosomes indicates that, of the two H3 tails in a nucleosome, the one on the side of the DNA end bound by PARP2 is closest to its active site (Bilokapic et al., 2020).
evidence: This is cited from prior structural work.

claim: PARP2 requires a terminal 5'-phosphate group for binding and activation.
source: Conveniently, PARP2 requires a terminal 5'-phosphate group for binding and activation (Langelier et al., 2014; Obaji et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: As few as three ADP-ribose units are sufficient for tight binding and full activation of ALC1.
source: All our attempts were aimed at limiting PAR chain length because it is known that as few as three ADP-ribose units are sufficient for tight binding and full activation of ALC1 (Singh et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from prior work.

claim: PARP1 indiscriminately produced PAR chains sufficiently long and heterogeneous to compromise cryo-EM image analysis.
source: While systematically assessing conditions with PARP1, we realized that it indiscriminately produced PAR chains sufficiently long and heterogeneous to compromise cryo-EM image analysis (Figure 1—figure supplement 3 and Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the Western blot and cryo-EM screening data in the figure supplements.

claim: PARP2 produced noticeably shorter PAR chains than PARP1.
source: We therefore turned to PARP2, as it produced noticeably shorter PAR chains (Figure 1—figure supplement 3) and yielded higher-quality particles (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the Western blot data in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: High concentrations of HPF1 tend to limit the elongation of PAR chains.
source: We noticed that high concentrations of HPF1 tend to limit the elongation of PAR chains, a phenomenon also recently reported, investigated in detail, and exploited by others (Langelier et al., 2021; Mohapatra et al., 2021).
evidence: This is an observation from the authors' experiments and supported by citations to recent work.

claim: A cryo-EM map of the ATPase domain of ALC1 bound to the nucleosome was obtained at 4.8 Å global resolution.
source: Despite a high level of conformational heterogeneity in our dataset (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), we could isolate a set of 5487 particles that yielded a map of the ATPase domain of ALC1 bound to the nucleosome with a global resolution of 4.8 Å (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and Table 1).
evidence: This is a primary structural finding demonstrated by the cryo-EM data.

claim: The 4.8 Å resolution map displays clear secondary structure elements allowing model building.
source: Nevertheless, this resolution is sufficient for the map to display clear secondary structure elements, allowing model building (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the cryo-EM map and atomic model shown in Figure 2.

claim: The ATPase motor of ALC1 is tightly bound to the nucleosomal DNA at superhelical location 2 (SHL2).
source: The map reveals an ATPase motor tightly bound to the nucleosomal DNA at superhelical location (SHL) 2 (Figure 2A,B), where the second major groove faces the histone octamer when numbering DNA turns starting at the nucleosome dyad (reviewed in McGinty and Tan, 2015; Zhou et al., 2019).
evidence: This is shown by the cryo-EM structure in Figure 2.

claim: Chd1, ISWI, and SWI/SNF-type remodelers all translocate on nucleosomal DNA at SHL2.
source: Chd1, ISWI, and SWI/SNF-type remodelers all translocate on nucleosomal DNA at this SHL2 site (Deindl et al., 2013; McKnight et al., 2011; Saha et al., 2005; Schwanbeck et al., 2004; Zofall et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: The C-terminal ATPase lobe of ALC1 interacts with the N-terminal tail of histone H4.
source: The map also shows a clear interaction of the C-terminal ATPase lobe with the N-terminal tail of histone H4 (Figure 2C–F).
evidence: This is shown by the cryo-EM structure in Figure 2C-F.

claim: Interaction with the H4 tail is conserved across almost all chromatin remodelers structurally characterized to date.
source: Both of these features are conserved across almost all chromatin remodelers structurally characterized to date (Armache et al., 2019; Chittori et al., 2019; Farnung et al., 2020; Farnung et al., 2017; Meijing et al., 2019; Liu et al., 2017a; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2018; Wagner et al., 2020; Yan et al., 2019; Ye et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior structural studies.

claim: The ATPase motor of ALC1 aligns optimally with the ADP-BeF3-bound conformations of Snf2 and Isw1.
source: The ATPase motor of ALC1 aligns optimally with the ADP-BeF3-bound conformations of Snf2 and Isw1, compared to their conformations in the presence of ADP or in the absence of any ligand (for Snf2), consistent with our use of this ligand to induce the active conformation of the motor.
evidence: This is demonstrated by structural comparison shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The ATPase motor of ALC1 is most similar to that of its closest homologue CHD4.
source: The ATPase motor of ALC1 is otherwise most similar to that of its closest homologue CHD4.
evidence: This is demonstrated by structural comparison shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The cryo-EM map does not show density for the macro domain of ALC1 or PAR chains on the nucleosome in the active state.
source: Notably, our map does not show density for either the macro domain of ALC1 or PAR chains on the nucleosome, most likely due to their extreme conformational flexibility in the active state (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-EM map with an interpretation provided.

claim: The average map from consensus 3D refinement displays clear density for an interaction between ALC1 and the nucleosome acidic patch.
source: However, the average map from a consensus 3D refinement of all 43,698 particles displays clear density for an interaction between ALC1 and the nucleosome acidic patch (Figure 3A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1), confirming at the structural level and in the context of ALC1fl our previous finding that the acidic patch is important for remodeling by ALC1 (Lehmann et al., 2020).
evidence: This is shown by the consensus cryo-EM map in Figure 3A and supported by citation to prior work.

claim: The consensus map features density assigned to the macro domain.
source: Moreover, this map also features density that we assign to the macro domain (Figure 3A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is shown by the consensus cryo-EM map in Figure 3A.

claim: The macro domain density makes contact with the ATPase motor.
source: this density makes contact with the ATPase motor, in agreement with the previously reported ATPase motor-macro domain interaction (Lehmann et al., 2017; Singh et al., 2017).
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-EM map supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The macro domain density resides on the side of ALC1 directed towards SHL1 where the N-terminal tail of H3 emerges.
source: Moreover, the density resides on the side of ALC1 directed towards SHL1 where the N-terminal tail of H3 emerges from the two DNA gyres of the nucleosome.
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-EM map.

claim: The macro domain is positioned at a location compatible with binding to PAR chains at the main PARylation site of the nucleosome.
source: The macro domain would thus be positioned at a location compatible with binding to PAR chains at the main PARylation site of the nucleosome (Bonfiglio et al., 2017).
evidence: This is inferred from the position of the macro domain density and supported by citation to prior work on PARylation sites.

claim: The distribution of particles in the latent space is smooth with no discrete clusters.
source: The distribution of particles in the latent space is smooth, with no discrete clusters, confirming the heterogeneity to be of a purely continuous conformational nature (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the cryoDRGN analysis shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The two opposite states along the first principal component correspond to ALC1 tightly bound to SHL2 and the H4 tail versus loosely bound to the nucleosomal DNA.
source: Principal component analysis of the Z values assigned to all particles revealed that the two opposite states along the first principal component of variability correspond to a state with ALC1 tightly bound to SHL2 and the H4 tail (same state described in Figure 2) and a state in which the ATPase domain is only loosely bound to the nucleosomal DNA (Videos 1–3).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the cryoDRGN analysis and shown in the videos.

claim: States with a wide-open ATPase domain conformation were detected.
source: Strikingly, we detected states in which the two ATPase lobes are splayed apart in a wide-open conformation (Figure 3B,C), similar to the auto-inhibited ATPase motor conformation inferred from SAXS and cross-linking experiments performed in the absence of a nucleosome (Lehmann et al., 2017).
evidence: This is shown by the cryoDRGN-generated maps in Figure 3B,C and supported by citation to prior work.

claim: The ATPase domain samples the nucleosomal DNA around SHL2, approximately from SHL1 to SHL3.
source: While the ATPase domain adopts its closed conformation and becomes tightly bound to SHL2, it also samples the nucleosomal DNA around SHL2, approximately from SHL1 to SHL3 (Figure 4, Videos 5 and 6).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the cryoDRGN analysis shown in Figure 4 and the videos.

claim: States with an open, loosely bound ATPase domain feature an interaction with the nucleosome acidic patch.
source: The states with an open, loosely bound ATPase domain also feature an interaction with the nucleosome acidic patch (Figure 4 and Video 5).
evidence: This is shown by the cryoDRGN-generated maps in Figure 4 and Video 5.

claim: The acidic patch interaction and macro domain densities progressively fade away as the ATPase domain transitions to the tightly bound state.
source: Both the acidic patch interaction and the macro domain densities progressively fade away as the ATPase domain transitions to the tightly bound state (Figure 4D–G, Video 5), indicating that the macro domain and linker occupy less constrained positions when the ATPase domain is in its active conformation.
evidence: This is shown by the cryoDRGN-generated maps in Figure 4D-G and Video 5.

claim: States with density connecting the nucleosome and macro domain at a location consistent with the PARylated H3 tail were detected.
source: We could further detect states with density connecting the nucleosome and macro domain, at a location consistent with the PARylated H3 tail (Figure 4C; also detected in an independent training run, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown by the cryoDRGN-generated map in Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The interaction between the C-terminal ATPase lobe and the H4 tail is detected in most states, including some with a loosely bound ATPase domain.
source: Finally, the interaction between the C-terminal ATPase lobe of ALC1 and the N-terminal tail of histone H4 is detected in most states, including some in which the ATPase domain is otherwise loosely bound to the DNA (Video 6).
evidence: This is shown by the cryoDRGN analysis in Video 6.

claim: The H4 tail interaction plays a role in recognition in addition to stimulating catalytic activity.
source: This suggests that this interaction plays a role in recognition, in addition to stimulating the catalytic activity of the ATPase domain as previously shown for other remodelers (Clapier and Cairns, 2012; Hwang et al., 2014; Ludwigsen et al., 2017; Markert et al., 2021; Racki et al., 2014).
evidence: This is inferred from the structural data and supported by citations to prior work on other remodelers.

claim: Nucleosome sliding by ALC1 followed Michaelis-Menten kinetics when PAR chains were attached to PARP1 but not to the nucleosome.
source: When PAR chains were attached to PARP1 but not to the nucleosome (in the absence of HPF1), the sliding reaction followed Michaelis–Menten kinetics with a KM of 30.7 nM and a Vmax of 0.11 (a.u.) (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the sliding assay data in Figure 5B.

claim: Nucleosome sliding did not follow Michaelis-Menten kinetics when PAR chains were attached to the nucleosome.
source: Unexpectedly, this was not the case when PAR chains were attached to the nucleosome (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the sliding assay data in Figure 5B.

claim: Asymmetric nucleosome PARylation likely results in two binding sites for ALC1 with different affinities.
source: One likely explanation is that the 63-N-0 end-positioned nucleosomes were preferentially PARylated on the H3 tail proximal to the short DNA end, since the PARP1 molecule bound at the end of the 63 bp linker DNA is too far away to reach the other H3 tail (approximately 214.2 Å away, equivalent to twice the diameter of a nucleosome and therefore too long to be spanned by even a fully extended H3 tail). Asymmetric nucleosome PARylation would result in two binding sites for ALC1 with different affinities: the PARylated side at SHL+2 with high affinity for ALC1, and the unmodified side at SHL-2 with lower affinity for ALC1.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors to explain the non-Michaelis-Menten kinetics.

claim: PARylation of the nucleosome enhanced sliding rates by approximately 2.5-fold at low concentrations of ALC1.
source: PARylation of the nucleosome did not affect the rate of sliding observed at saturating concentrations of ALC1, but instead enhanced sliding rates by ~2.5-fold at low concentrations of ALC1 (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the sliding assay data in Figure 5B.

claim: The overall fastest sliding rate observed in the presence of HPF1 occurs at approximately 30 nM ALC1.
source: The overall fastest sliding rate observed in the presence of HPF1 occurs at ~30 nM ALC1, which matches the KM value determined in the absence of HPF1.
evidence: This is an observation from the sliding assay data in Figure 5B.

claim: Remodeling by ALC1 was consistently slower at all concentrations tested when using ALC1fl R611A/S612A with WT nucleosomes.
source: Remodeling by ALC1 was consistently slower at all concentrations of ALC1 tested when using ALC1fl R611A/S612A with WT nucleosomes (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 2)
evidence: This is demonstrated by the sliding assay data in Figure 5C.

claim: Remodeling by ALC1 was consistently slower when using ALC1fl with APM nucleosomes.
source: Remodeling by ALC1 was consistently slower at all concentrations of ALC1 tested when using... ALC1fl with APM nucleosomes (Figure 5D, Figure 5—figure supplement 3)
evidence: This is demonstrated by the sliding assay data in Figure 5D.

claim: Remodeling by ALC1 was consistently slower when using ALC1fl with gH4 nucleosomes.
source: Remodeling by ALC1 was consistently slower at all concentrations of ALC1 tested when using... ALC1fl with gH4 nucleosomes (Figure 5E, Figure 5—figure supplement 4; see also Table 3).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the sliding assay data in Figure 5E.

claim: The ATPase activity of ALC1 was stimulated to the same extent regardless of whether HPF1 was present in the PARylation reaction.
source: Interestingly, the ATPase activity of ALC1 was stimulated to the same extent regardless of whether the PARylation reaction prior to the addition of ATP contained HPF1 or not.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the ATPase assay data in Figure 5F.

claim: The faster sliding rate for nucleosomes PARylated with HPF1 at low ALC1 concentrations was not due to more rapid ATP hydrolysis.
source: This suggests that the faster sliding rate for nucleosomes PARylated with HPF1 observed with low concentrations of ALC1 (Figure 5B) was not due to more rapid ATP hydrolysis, but rather can be explained by a higher affinity of ALC1 for the PARylated side of the nucleosome.
evidence: This is inferred from the ATPase assay data showing equal ATP hydrolysis rates.

claim: Disruption of the acidic patch interaction by the R611A/S612A mutation caused a decrease in ATPase activity by a factor of approximately 3.5.
source: Both the disruption of the acidic patch interaction by the R611A/S612 mutation of ALC1 and the deletion of the H4 tail caused a decrease in ATPase activity by a factor of ~3.5
evidence: This is demonstrated by the ATPase assay data in Figure 5F.

claim: Deletion of the H4 tail caused a decrease in ATPase activity by a factor of approximately 3.5.
source: Both the disruption of the acidic patch interaction by the R611A/S612 mutation of ALC1 and the deletion of the H4 tail caused a decrease in ATPase activity by a factor of ~3.5
evidence: This is demonstrated by the ATPase assay data in Figure 5F.

claim: The acidic patch and H4 tail both regulate ALC1 remodeling primarily by stimulating its ATPase activity.
source: suggesting that the acidic patch and the H4 tail both regulate ALC1 remodeling primarily by stimulating its ATPase activity.
evidence: This is inferred from the ATPase assay data showing reduced ATP hydrolysis when these interactions are disrupted.

claim: This is the first report of a PARylated nucleosome used for structure determination.
source: Structures of complexes containing post-translationally modified nucleosomes have been determined before (Anderson et al., 2019; Chatterjee et al., 2015; Hsu et al., 2019; Jang et al., 2019; Kasinath et al., 2021; Lu et al., 2008; Morgan et al., 2016; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2018; Valencia-Sánchez et al., 2021; Valencia-Sánchez et al., 2019; Wang et al., 2020b; Wang et al., 2020a; Wilson et al., 2016; Worden et al., 2020, Worden et al., 2019; Xue et al., 2019; Yao et al., 2019), but the present study is, to the best of our knowledge, the first report of a PARylated nucleosome used for structure determination.
evidence: This is stated by the authors based on their knowledge of the literature.

claim: ALC1 shares two conserved features with other remodelers: ATPase motor binding at SHL2 and C-ATPase lobe interaction with the H4 tail.
source: The structure revealed that ALC1 shares two conserved features with other remodelers: its ATPase motor binds to the nucleosomal DNA at SHL2, and the C-ATPase lobe interacts with the N-terminal tail of histone H4.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the cryo-EM structure and comparison with other remodelers.

claim: The interaction with the H4 tail was previously shown to be important for remodeling by ALC1 in vitro and in cells.
source: This interaction with the H4 tail was previously shown to be important for remodeling by ALC1, both in vitro using gH4 nucleosomes (Ahel et al., 2009) and in cells with the point mutations D377A and D381A in ALC1 (Verma et al., 2021; Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The slowest rate of ATP hydrolysis by ALC1fl stimulated by PARylated gH4 nucleosomes is almost twice as fast as the fastest rate by ALC1fl R860W stimulated by unmodified WT nucleosomes.
source: Remarkably, the slowest rate of ATP hydrolysis measured for ALC1fl stimulated by PARylated gH4 nucleosomes is almost twice as fast as the fastest rate of hydrolysis measured previously for the constitutively active ALC1fl R860W stimulated by unmodified WT nucleosomes (Lehmann et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a comparison of data from this study with prior work.

claim: The rate of hydrolysis by ALC1fl stimulated by PARylated WT nucleosomes is more than sixfold faster than that of ALC1fl R860W stimulated by unmodified WT nucleosomes.
source: Moreover, the rate of hydrolysis by ALC1fl stimulated by PARylated WT nucleosomes is more than sixfold faster than that of ALC1fl R860W stimulated by unmodified WT nucleosomes (Lehmann et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a comparison of data from this study with prior work.

claim: The bona fide substrate of ALC1 is a PARylated nucleosome, eliciting an ATP hydrolysis rate on par with that of Chd1.
source: This further emphasizes that the bona fide substrate of ALC1 is a PARylated nucleosome, eliciting an ATP hydrolysis rate on par with that of Chd1 (Hauk et al., 2010; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).
evidence: This is inferred from the ATPase data and supported by citations to prior work on Chd1.

claim: The R611A/S612A mutations reduce ATP hydrolysis by a similar factor of approximately 3.5-fold in both PARylated and unmodified nucleosome settings.
source: Despite these differences in the absolute rate of ATP hydrolysis between these reactions with PARylated or unmodified nucleosomes, the R611A/S612A mutations that disrupt the acidic patch interaction reduce ATP hydrolysis by a similar factor of ~3.5-fold in both settings.
evidence: This is a comparison of data from this study with prior work.

claim: A recent article reported the crystal structure of ALC1 in its auto-inhibited state and the cryo-EM structure of a constitutively active mutant cross-linked to an unmodified nucleosome.
source: While our manuscript was under review, an article was published that reported the crystal structure of ALC1 in its auto-inhibited state and the cryo-EM structure of a constitutively active mutant of ALC1 cross-linked to an unmodified nucleosome (Wang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a citation to concurrent work.

claim: The structure of ALC1 in the nucleosome-free state confirms the model of auto-inhibition proposed previously.
source: The structure of ALC1 in the nucleosome-free state confirms the model of auto-inhibition that was proposed previously (Lehmann et al., 2017; Singh et al., 2017) and shows good agreement with one of the states we observed here with ALC1 loosely bound to the nucleosome (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a comparison with concurrent work by Wang et al., 2021.

claim: The overall structure of the cross-linked complex between ALC1 and the nucleosome by Wang et al. agrees well with the findings in this study.
source: The overall structure of the cross-linked complex between ALC1 and the nucleosome by Wang et al. agrees well with our previous and present findings.
evidence: This is a comparison with concurrent work by Wang et al., 2021.

claim: In both this study and Wang et al., ALC1 binds the nucleosome at the same superhelical location and interacts with the H4 tail.
source: In both the structure we report here and the one by Wang et al., ALC1 binds the nucleosome at the same superhelical location and interacts with the H4 tail.
evidence: This is a comparison with concurrent work by Wang et al., 2021.

claim: The structure by Wang et al. could not resolve the macro domain of ALC1, most likely due to their use of an unmodified nucleosome.
source: The structure by Wang et al. could not resolve the macro domain of ALC1, most likely due to their use of an unmodified nucleosome (Wang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a comparison with concurrent work by Wang et al., 2021 with an interpretation.

claim: In this study's structure of ALC1 bound to a PARylated nucleosome, the macro domain was detected along with its dynamic interaction with the PARylated H3 tail.
source: In our structure of ALC1 bound to a PARylated nucleosome, we not only detected the macro domain but also its dynamic interaction with the PARylated H3 tail.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the cryoDRGN analysis showing macro domain density.

claim: Wang et al. found two arginine anchors, R611 and R614, in their structure.
source: Interestingly, Wang et al. found two arginine anchors, R611 and R614.
evidence: This is cited from concurrent work by Wang et al., 2021.

claim: In Wang et al.'s structure, R614 binds in a canonical Arg anchor mode while R611 adopts a variant Arg anchor binding mode.
source: In their structure, residue R614 of ALC1 binds to the acidic pocket formed by residues E61, D90, and E92 of histone H2A in a conformation termed 'canonical Arg anchor', while R611 adopts a 'variant Arg anchor' binding mode (reviewed in McGinty and Tan, 2021).
evidence: This is cited from concurrent work by Wang et al., 2021.

claim: In a previous structure by the authors, R611 was observed as the canonical Arg anchor.
source: In our previous structure of the regulatory linker segment of ALC1 cross-linked to a nucleosome, we observed residue R611 as the canonical Arg anchor (Lehmann et al., 2020).
evidence: This is cited from the authors' prior work.

claim: Different Arg anchor residues can occupy the canonical position in different structures of the same complex.
source: Such an interaction with the nucleosome acidic patch, involving different Arg anchor residues in different structures, occurred in at least one other instance. The BAH domain of Sir3 contains a stretch of several consecutive arginine residues. In two structures, residue R29 is the canonical Arg anchor (Armache et al., 2011; Arnaudo et al., 2013), while residue R30 (Wang et al., 2013) or R32 (Yang et al., 2013) occupies the canonical Arg anchor position in two other structures of the same complex.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior structural studies of Sir3.

claim: Asymmetric linker DNA length on the nucleosome construct appeared to bias PARylation towards sites closest to the short DNA end.
source: Of note, the asymmetric linker DNA length on the 63N-0 nucleosome construct used for sliding assays appeared to bias PARylation of histones towards the sites closest to the short DNA end, which in turn affected the directionality of nucleosome sliding by ALC1.
evidence: This is inferred from the sliding assay data showing non-Michaelis-Menten kinetics.

claim: This in vitro phenomenon may mimic the processing of a DNA break in vivo where PARP would preferentially PARylate target sites closest to the break.
source: This in vitro phenomenon may mimic the processing of a DNA break in vivo: in this context, PARP1 or PARP2 would bind to the break and preferentially PARylate target sites closest to it, which would in turn cause ALC1 to slide the PARylated histone octamer away from the DNA break, making it more accessible to downstream repair factors (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors based on their in vitro observations.

claim: Preferential PARylation of target sites closest to the DNA break would cause ALC1 to slide the nucleosome away from the break.
source: in this context, PARP1 or PARP2 would bind to the break and preferentially PARylate target sites closest to it, which would in turn cause ALC1 to slide the PARylated histone octamer away from the DNA break, making it more accessible to downstream repair factors (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors illustrated in Figure 6.

claim: Sliding the nucleosome away from the break would make it more accessible to downstream repair factors.
source: which would in turn cause ALC1 to slide the PARylated histone octamer away from the DNA break, making it more accessible to downstream repair factors (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors illustrated in Figure 6.

claim: The structural and biochemical analyses provide insight into the critical early steps by which ALC1 recognizes and engages PARylated nucleosomes for productive remodeling in damaged chromatin.
source: In conclusion, our structural and biochemical analyses provide a window into the critical early steps by which, in the context of damaged chromatin, ALC1 recognizes and engages PARylated nucleosomes for productive remodeling.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the study's contributions.

claim: This work sheds light on the intricate regulatory mechanisms that control the activity of the ALC1 remodeler.
source: Our work sheds light on the intricate regulatory mechanisms that control the activity of the ALC1 remodeler, which is emerging as an important therapeutic option in homologous recombination-deficient cancers.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the study's contributions and significance.
